t: Mike Johnson: ‘Leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong’
lede: Republican House speaker not running for re-election contrasts sharply with president who avoids accountability

img.cap: Mike Johnson said he decided to leave his leadership role ‘pretty quickly after election night’. Photograph: Alex Wong/Getty Images

p: In his first interview since the

, said that the Republican party’s crushing losses during the 3 November elections prompted his decision to step away from party leadership.
“Leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong,” Johnson
on Fox News on Saturday.
The Republican leader, who informed aides on 4 November that he would not seek re-election for House leadership, said on Saturday that he reached the decision “pretty quickly after election night”.

“We worked around the clock, left it all on the field to win. We had to defy history, as you and I both know, it’s only happened twice in 90 years, but we did everything that we could to make that happen,” Johnson said. “But, you know, this was the a year where history was not defied …

“We don’t like the results,” he said. “But, real leadership, I’ve always believed, you lead from the front, and leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong whether it’s individually deserved or not, that’s part of it …
“I’m going to remain in this fight, but from a role different than as minority leader in the next Congress,” he added.

It stood in sharp contrast to the reaction of Donald Trump, who has deflected all responsibility for the devastating losses suffered by his party, including defeats for at least 10 Republican Senate candidates in states where he held rallies in the closing weeks of the campaign. That number could rise to 11, should Alaska’s incumbent Republican senator, Dan Sullivan, be defeated.

Democrats have not yet voted on who will lead their party in the House and Senate when the new Congress convenes in January. The representative Hakeem Jeffries, of New York, currently serves as House minority leader for the Democrats, and is expected to become the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, while the senator Chuck Schumer, also of New York, currently leads Senate Democrats.
